LO reported that the customer services team had received a higher than expected number of calls about discoloured water following the flushing works in the Elm Park area. Most calls were resolved with a standard leaflet drop, but some residents had called back to say the water was still discoloured after 24 hours.

SP confirmed that the flushing schedule had been amended to include an additional rinse on the affected mains. He said the water quality team had been attending follow-up samples and that the issue appeared to be resolving. SP will provide LO with a summary of the affected postcodes so that the customer services team can respond to any further enquiries with accurate information.

LO asked whether the leaflet template needed updating, as some residents had said the wording was unclear about what to do if discolouration persisted. CW agreed that the template should be reviewed and asked LO to circulate a draft for comment by 16/02.

**4. Ashford Road Valve Replacement – Update**

CW provided an update on the Ashford Road valve replacement. The contractor had confirmed that the site compound would be set up on 19/02, with the main works scheduled to start on 26/02. The lane closure is still planned for 24/02 as previously discussed.

DK confirmed that he had chased the lane closure confirmation from the local authority and expected to receive it by 23/02. He will update the tracker as soon as it arrives.

CW reminded the team that the valve replacement would require a planned supply interruption for properties on Ashford Road and the adjacent streets. LO said the customer services team had already been briefed and that notification letters would be sent out on 14/02. She asked whether there were any properties that would need a longer notice period. CW said he would check with the contractor and confirm by 12/02.

**Operational Meeting Minutes – 06/02/2024 (continued)**

**6. Water Quality – Iron and Manganese Complaints**

CW opened item 6 by referring back to the discolouration issues reported in the Lowfield and
Brampton areas last month. He said the flushing programme in Lowfield had been completed on
02/02 and initial results were positive. LO confirmed that customer contacts related to
discolouration had dropped from 14 in the week commencing 22/01 to 6 in the week commencing
29/01. She cautioned that this was still above the seasonal average and that the team should
not assume the issue was resolved.

MB noted that raw water samples taken from the inlet at Lowfield on 31/01 showed iron at
0.32 mg/L, which was above the usual range for that source. He said the elevated reading was
likely due to the recent high flows following the storm on 28/01 and that he expected levels
to return to normal within a week. CW asked MB to keep a log of all iron and manganese
readings from Lowfield and to report back at the next meeting.

DK raised a question about the Brampton complaints. He said that two customers on Elm Grove
had reported brown water on 03/02, which was after the Brampton rinse had been completed. LO
confirmed that she had spoken to both customers and that the discolouration had cleared
within a few hours. She said she would monitor whether any further complaints came in from
that street. CW said that if there was a repeat, the team should consider a targeted flush of
the Elm Grove dead-end main.

**7. Pressure Monitoring – Station Road**

DK reported on the pressure monitoring work that had been agreed at the previous meeting. He
said that two temporary loggers had been installed on Station Road on 05/02 and that initial
data showed pressures within the expected range during daytime hours. However, he noted that
overnight pressures between 00:00 and 05:00 were consistently lower than the modelled
predictions, by around 0.4 bar. He said this could indicate a partially closed valve or a
leak on the network and that he would carry out a night-time survey on 12/02 to investigate.

CW asked whether the low overnight pressures could affect the Ashford Road works scheduled
for later this month. DK said he did not think so, as the two areas were on different supply
zones, but he would confirm once the survey was complete. MB added that the North Hill
reservoir inspection in March would also need to be considered in relation to pressure
management, as taking the tank out of service would reduce storage capacity and could lower
pressures in the zone during peak demand. DK said he would liaise with MB to ensure the
pressure survey results were shared before the inspection dates were confirmed.

**8. Health and Safety – Near Miss Reporting**

CW moved to item 8 and reminded the team that the monthly near miss report for January had
been circulated by email on 05/02. He said the total number of reported near misses had
increased from 9 in December to 14 in January, which he considered a positive sign that
reporting culture was improving. He highlighted two specific near misses that required
follow-up.

The first involved a contractor working near a live water main on 24/01. The contractor had
been carrying out excavation work without a valid permit to dig, and the incident was spotted
by a BTWS supervisor during a routine site visit. CW said the contractor had been stopped
immediately and that a full investigation had been carried out. The contractor had since
provided evidence that their permit had expired the previous day and that they had not
realised it needed renewing. CW said the contractor had been issued a formal warning and that
their permit would be subject to additional checks for the next three months.
